claims.text: Integrating POD into TOR-TILD will significantly reduce the computational cost of fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic calculations for multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
The POD-integrated workflow will retain the fidelity of vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling effects.
CrCoNi and CoCrFeNiTax are intended target high-entropy-alloy systems for the proposed method.
Above the Debye temperature, vibrational and anharmonic entropy contributions are critical in both solid and liquid high-entropy alloys.
POD applied to short molecular-dynamics trajectory segments can extract the dominant vibrational eigenmodes.
A reduced set of POD modes can reconstruct the relevant free-energy landscape with substantially fewer degrees of freedom.
Adaptive sensitivity analysis can ensure that retained POD modes capture crucial anharmonic and electron–vibration coupling effects.
The dominant POD modes encapsulate most entropy-relevant atomic motion.
The dominant POD modes capture essential anharmonic distortions and electron–vibration interactions.
POD principal components isolate the collective motions contributing most significantly to free energy.
Sensitivity-guided calibration of the retained mode count will allow reconstructed free energies to reflect vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration effects accurately.
Reduced-mode reconstruction will dramatically decrease the number of molecular-dynamics steps required.
The hybrid method will produce free energies and derived fusion properties within approximately 0.05 eV/atom of full TOR-TILD or explicit AIMD results.
The hybrid method will achieve computational speedups of approximately 100–1000 times for multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Full AIMD and TOR-TILD free-energy workflows are computationally intensive, especially for multicomponent alloys.
The proposed method is applicable to high-entropy alloys containing 4–10 elements.
The proposed temperature range extends from slightly above the Debye temperature to melting conditions.
A deviation greater than approximately 0.05 eV/atom in solid–liquid free-energy differences or greater than ±50 K in fusion temperature will falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The stated composition boundary is 4–10 elements, but CrCoNi, repeatedly given as a representative target, contains only three elements.
